svg.aria-label: How to write தமிழ்: 5 parts, த, ம, ி, ழ, ், one after another
svg.title: Writing தமிழ்
svg.desc: 5 parts written one after another: த, ம, ி, ழ, ் (tamil). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which is not always the order they are typed: a vowel sign written to the left of its consonant comes before it. Each vowel sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansTamil-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: த: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 3, த (University of Texas at Austin), p. 192 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ம: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 1 (Univ. of Texas at Austin) <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ி: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 37 (ி, i sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Tamil writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>; ழ: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 7, ழ (University of Texas at Austin), p. 193 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ்: Abhinaya Rajarajan, Varai (Swift Student Challenge 2026), reference drawings recorded by hand for the 18 Tamil consonants with pulli, க் to ன் (repository commit 952294fa, no licence: facts only) <https://github.com/abhinayaRajarajan/varai>. Source notes on variation: த: Module 3 identifies த as the dental stop and asks learners to write it. Appendix I's final Frame 3 row numbers seven hand-movements: 1–2 for the upper frame, 3–4 for the broad right bowl, 5–6 for the compact left loop, and 7 for the leftward tail. Native writers draw த as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows the seven movements in order without lifting. Because the manual numbers the right bowl before the left loop, the pen retraces the right bowl to reach the loop and again to reach the tail. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 88% of the 266 stored prototypes of த are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline. ம: Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation; there is no single national stroke-order standard. This is one attested order. ி: The recognizer stores native Tamil writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 205 of the 206 stored prototypes of the i sign are one pen-down stroke. In 161 of those 205 the pen starts at the tip of the hook and first moves up; 200 turn clockwise, over the top to the right; 152 end at the foot of the stem. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. ழ: Appendix I Frame 7 numbers six movements: 1–3 form the left body and bar, 4–5 the inner upright and broad right bowl, and 6 the lower hook. Native writers draw them as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows them in order without lifting. The bundled Noto Sans Tamil print face simplifies the source's looped left body and high bar into a retraced upright with a low crossbar that runs straight into the bowl's foot, so movement 3 carries on round the foot and up the bowl's right side, movement 4 comes back left over the top into the inner upright, and movement 5 descends it into the stem below the baseline. The face joins the hook to that stem only at the hook's far end, so movement 6 runs round the hook to its tip and comes back round it into the short tail. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 97% of the 182 stored prototypes of ழ are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order. ்: One writer's recorded reference drawings, stored in the order they were drawn. In all 18 the consonant body is one stroke and the puḷḷi is a separate second stroke, made after the body is complete, so it costs one pen lift. Its centre sits above the body at 0.47 to 0.65 of the body's width (0.54 for க்). An earlier reading of Info-farmer's Writing Tamil animations of the consonants on Wikimedia Commons, which show each consonant with its puḷḷi, also places the dot after the body. Confidence is medium: one recorded writer, and only stroke count, order and the dot's bounding box were read; the dot is about 10 by 13 canvas units, too small to say which way the pen moved, so the short downward dab drawn here is not a claim. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil disc, which the font centres at 0.43 to 0.60 of the consonant's width, a little left of where this writer put it. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 parts, one after another
Part 1 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 7 movements
Part 2 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 5 movements
Part 3 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 4 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 6 movements
Part 1: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 3, த (University of Texas at Austin), p. 192
Part 2: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 1 (Univ. of Texas at Austin)
Part 3: stroke order after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 37 (ி, i sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native
Part 4: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 7, ழ (University of Texas at Austin), p. 193
Part 5: stroke order after Abhinaya Rajarajan, Varai (Swift Student Challenge 2026), reference drawings recorded by hand for the 18 Tamil consonants with pulli, க் to ன் (repository
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
